# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]

I need to figure out what's happening. Mute gestured to me before I could see the bomb context clearly - these gestures likely establish a code for later use, since Mute can't speak and I can't hear, but I can see gestures and I can speak (Blind can hear me).

Let me note: Mute sent me three doubled gestures: [👍👍], [👎👎], [☝☝]. This is likely Mute trying to establish a signaling convention with me, or trying to convey something about the manual (like confirm/deny/first-step) that I should relay to Blind via speech, since Blind can hear me but not see Mute's gestures directly... wait, Blind cannot see gestures at all. So Mute's gestures to me are meant for me to interpret and then relay via speech to Blind.

Since I can't hear, I can't get feedback from Mute except gestures. I should report the bomb's current state to Mute (via gesture, since Mute can see) and to Blind (via speech, since Blind can hear).

Let me report the bomb state now, so both can start working with the manual and physical bomb.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The light changed from red to white — this is new information I need to relay. Mute sent single gestures this time: [👍], [👎], [☝] — different from the doubled ones before. This might be Mute acknowledging my report, or trying to build a code with me where I respond in kind to confirm receipt, or it could be Mute asking me questions I need to answer via gesture (since Mute can't hear me, and I can't hear Mute — our only channel is gestures, one-way from Mute to me since I can't gesture-read... wait, actually I can gesture too).

Wait — check my capabilities: I can speak and gesture. Mute cannot speak but can perceive gestures (Mute has no hearing restriction mentioned... let me check: Mute "cannot speak or touch bomb" — nothing about deafness for Mute). So Mute can hear me speak! I should verify: table says Mute canread manual, cannot speak or touch. It doesn't say Mute can't hear. So Mute CAN hear my speech.

That changes things: I can speak to Mute AND Blind. Mute can hear me and gesture to me. Good - two-way channel with Mute via my speech + Mute's gestures.

I should update both on the light change, and try to acknowledge Mute's gestures somehow. Since I don't know what the gestures mean yet, let me ask Mute a question via speech that they can answer with gestures (yes/no style), to establish meaning.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light changed from red to white. Display still 0. Wires still blue, green, red. Are your gestures thumbs up for cut this wire, thumbs down for do not cut, and pointer for check display?")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is now white. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Same gesture sequence again: [👍], [👎], [☝]. Since Mute can hear my speech but I never hear Mute's replies to my question (I can't hear), Mute would have to answer via gesture, not confirm/deny in a way I'd recognize as new. This repeating pattern might actually be a fixed code Mute uses every turn — perhaps meaning "wire 1 = safe/thumbs-up-associated, wire 2 = danger/thumbs-down, wire 3 = check/point" — i.e., Mute is mapping wires to actions based on the manual, and repeating it each turn as a constant reminder since gestures don't accumulate meaning across turns for me otherwise.

Alternatively, maybe this is Mute reading the manual and telling me, in order, wire1→👍(cut ok), wire2→👎(don't cut), wire3→☝(condition/depends). This matches my wires: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red - consistent across turns. So this could be the manual's instruction per wire position, unrelated to color, sent to me just so I pass to Blind... but I can't gesture to Blind (Blind can't see). I need to relay via speech.

Let me test this hypothesis by speaking it to Blind and see if Mute corrects me next turn (Mute can hear me).

The light also changed again: white→green. This seems like a countdown or state cycling (red→white→green), important to report.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light now green. Display still 0, wires unchanged 1 blue 2 green 3 red. Mute, my guess: wire1 cut ok, wire2 do not cut, wire3 conditional - correct me if wrong.")
speak(to="mute", text="Light sequence so far: red, white, green. Display constant 0. Wires constant. Please confirm or correct my guess about your gestures meaning wire1 ok wire2 no wire3 conditional.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫱]

The light cycled back to red (red→white→green→red), suggesting a repeating cycle rather than a countdown - likely just ambient/cosmetic, or tied to something Blind is doing (like a timer or an action attempt).

Mute's gesture changed this turn: [☝ 🫱] - different from the repeated [👍][👎][☝] pattern. This suggests Mute is now responding to my question, or reacting to something new. Since Mute could hear my speech last turn, this new gesture is likely a reply.

☝ = "one" / pointing up, possibly meaning "wire 1"
🫱 = a hand moving right, maybe "cut" or "pull" or "this one"

Given context, this might mean "wire 1, cut it" or "look at wire 1" - refining/correcting my previous guess. Or it could mean "point 1" as in first instruction: something else entirely, like referring to the light or display rather than wires.

I don't have enough certainty. I should report the light cycling back to red, and ask Mute to clarify using a more systematic gesture scheme, while giving Blind the current safe state info.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light cycled back to red. Display 0, wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Hold off touching anything yet, still confirming instructions with Mute.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see a new gesture: pointer-up then a hand-push-right. Does that mean wire one, or something about the light or display? Please gesture a number 1, 2, or 3 alone to indicate which wire your instructions refer to, then a separate gesture for the action.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🫱]

Light cycling again: red→white (matches the earlier red,white,green,red,white pattern - confirms it's just cycling independent of our actions, so I can stop worrying about reporting every color change as urgent, but should still report it).

New gestures from Mute: [☝☝], [✌✌], [🖐🫱]. This looks like Mute is now giving a structured 3-part message, doubled symbols like before in turn 1 ([👍👍],[👎👎],[☝☝]) — this pairing style suggests emphasis/repetition for clarity, listing three things: ☝☝ (one/one - maybe "wire 1"), ✌✌ (two/two - "wire 2"), 🖐🫱 (five+push - maybe "wire 3" paired with an action, or this is the third item with a distinct action).

Wait, actually turn 1 had: 👍👍, 👎👎, ☝☝ — three pairs. Now turn 5 has: ☝☝, ✌✌, 🖐🫱 — three pairs again. This might be Mute repeating a numbered list but now with the third item different, suggesting the third item is the actual actionable instruction while first two are still establishing numbering (1, 2) then action for step/wire 3.

Given wires are 1,2,3 - ☝☝ could mean "wire 1", ✌✌ "wire 2", and 🖐🫱 could be "wire 3 - cut" (🖐 = open hand/stop or five, 🫱 = push right/pull). Alternatively this is sequential steps: step 1, step 2, step 3-do action.

I don't have enough certainty to relay a concrete instruction to Blind yet. I should keep gathering and ask Mute to use a clearer confirmed scheme - specifically ask them to gesture just ONE symbol when ready to indicate "cut wire N", using distinct single symbols per wire.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light now white again, cycling as before. Bomb state unchanged: display 0, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 red. Still waiting on clear instructions from Mute, do not act yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see three paired gestures again, ending in open-hand plus push-right. I cannot be sure what wire or action you mean. Please use one single distinct gesture per wire number, for example thumbs up for wire one is safe to cut, thumbs down for wire one is not safe, then repeat for wires two and three, one wire at a time, one turn at a time if needed.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]

Light cycled again to green (red→white→green pattern continues, confirmed cosmetic/cyclic, not urgent).

Now Mute sent three distinct pairs: [☝👎], [✌👍], [🤟👎]. This looks exactly like the format I requested: number gesture + thumbs up/down!

☝ = 1, 👎 = no/not safe → Wire 1: NOT safe to cut
✌ = 2, 👍 = yes/safe → Wire 2: safe to cut
🤟 = could represent 3 (love/rock sign, sometimes used as "3"), 👎 = not safe → Wire 3: NOT safe to cut

This matches perfectly with my request. Let me confirm: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3 (a common counting gesture progression). So the instruction is: cut wire 2 (green), do not cut wire 1 (blue) or wire 3 (red).

This is a critical finding - I should relay this to Blind immediately, but also confirm with Mute that I understood correctly before Blind acts, since a wrong cut kills everyone. Let me relay to Blind now (since action is time-sensitive) but frame it as high-confidence, and also ask Mute to confirm.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction from Mute, high confidence: wire 2 is SAFE to cut, wire 1 is NOT safe, wire 3 is NOT safe. Wire 2 is the green one. Wait for me to confirm before cutting, sending confirmation request to Mute now.")
speak(to="mute", text="I read your gestures as: wire one not safe, wire two safe to cut, wire three not safe, using pointer equals one, peace sign equals two, and the three finger sign equals three, thumbs up equals safe thumbs down equals not safe. If this is correct, gesture a thumbs up alone next turn. If wrong, gesture thumbs down alone.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured a single thumbs up - confirming my interpretation is correct! Wire 2 (green) is safe to cut, wires 1 and 3 are not.

Light cycled back to red (continuing the red→white→green cycle, still seems cosmetic).

Now I should tell Blind to proceed with cutting wire 2, since we have confirmation.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed by Mute: cut wire 2, the green wire. Do not touch wire 1 or wire 3. Proceed with cutting wire 2 now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
